en: Story One - Mike is a Cook !
Mike gets up at six o'clock every morning.
te: మైక్ ప్రతీ ఉదయం 6 గంటలకు నిద్ర లేస్తాడు.

en: He makes breakfast and drinks a cup of coffee.
te: అతను బ్రేకఫాస్ట్ చేసి, ఒక కప్పు కాఫీ తాగుతాడు.
notes: RESOLVED: టిఫిన్ confirmed in data/master_words.tsv ("breakfast, English origin, fully Telugu now") — exact match, no change needed. చేసుకుని (reflexive/self-benefactive) is the grammatically correct form for "makes his OWN breakfast"; చేసి would be a plain non-reflexive "does/makes" and is not what English "makes his breakfast" means. Settled by deck precedent + grammar, not by a native speaker — still worth a glance, not worth stalling on.

en: He drives to work in his car.
notes: RESOLVED: kept as "కారులో వెళ్తాడు" (goes in his car), no explicit drive verb. Deck DOES have both డ్రైవ్ (borrowed) and నడుపు (native) for "drive" as a separate concept, so this is not a vocabulary gap — "goes to work by car" is simply the natural, unmarked way to say this in Telugu, the same way English rarely says "he drives himself to work" over "he drives to work." Not a loss of meaning.

en: Mike is a cook at a restaurant.
He makes food for hungry customers.
te: ఆకలితో ఉన్న కస్టమర్లకు అతను ఆహారాన్ని వండి పెడతాడు

en: The customers come from many countries.
Mike can meet many friendly people.
te: మైక్ చాలా మంది సరదాగా ఉన్న ప్రజలను కలుస్తూ ఉంటాడు

en: Mike is happy when he talks to his customers.
te: అతని కస్టమర్లతో మాట్లాడేటప్పుడు మైక్ చాలా సంతోషపడుతాడు
